column3: “Utterance” is rendered “declares,” and “the pleasant one of the songs of Israel” as “the sweet psalmist of Israel.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “righteously” for the terse Hebrew “one who rules over man, righteous.”
NASB supplies “Is as,” and arranges the terse Hebrew (“from brightness, from rain, grass from the earth”) into a full sentence.
The Hebrew “for not so is my house with God” is read as a question, “is not my house so with God?”
Close to the Hebrew.
“At the dwelling” is rendered “in their place”; the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew is difficult; NASB follows readings close to 1 Chr 11:11 (“chief of the captains,” “he was called Adino the Eznite”) and supplies “because of.”
“The son of Ahohi” is rendered “the Ahohite,” and “went up” as “had withdrawn.”
“Deliverance” is rendered “victory,” and NASB supplies “the slain.”
“To Lehi” (or “into a troop”) is rendered “into a troop”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Delivered it” is rendered “defended it,” and “deliverance” as “victory.”
“To the harvest” is rendered “in the harvest time,” and “a community” as “the troop.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Desired” is rendered “had a craving,” and “Who will give me to drink” as “Oh that someone would give me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “Shall I drink,” and renders “went with their lives” as “went in jeopardy of their lives.”
The Hebrew written text reads “chief of the three”; NASB has “chief of the thirty,” as in some manuscripts. NASB supplies “and killed them.”
The Hebrew reads “more than the three”; NASB has “most honored of the thirty.”
“Two lion-like men (Ariel) of Moab” is rendered “the two sons of Ariel of Moab”; the meaning is uncertain.
“A man of appearance” (written text) is rendered “an impressive man,” and “staff” as “club.”
